approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent molecular prior and chooses its prepared checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid, connected, distinct molecular yield, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts an adaptable copy of that prior and an accepted-only archive; trajectory-balance updates with a learned normalizer and fixed-prior regularization transfer real graph feedback into later neural sampling. One direct neural batch alternates with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population and supply a protected descendant at the first graph handoff. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations construct temporary novel offspring pools, and accepted-score fingerprint posterior function draws choose the remaining evaluations. The atom-replacement mutation currently changes one element at one site, so moving a ring nitrogen while retaining composition requires multiple separately sampled substitutions.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with a direct positional exchange between a pyridine-like nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same aromatic six-member ring. The exchange moves the nitrogen while preserving the formula, ring connectivity and substituent attachment positions, making a new local arrangement available in one edit. Earlier Children in this lineage changed prior preparation, replay, flow credit or neural sampling. This Child changes graph generation. A previous graph-walk experiment established that this exchange can yield scored positional isomers but exposed very few of them and missed its score target; the new question is whether the Parent's larger temporary pools and posterior selection turn that same positional channel into useful accepted descendants.

hypothesis: Extend the existing graph replace_atom option menu with a direct formula-preserving exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, retaining the ring connectivity and substituent attachment framework.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per objective. The molecules include linked and fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, aryl sulfonamides, lactams, ethers, imidates and fluorinated urea/hydrazine chains. This is broad chemical exploration with concentrated upper-score families, rather than a shortage of rings or nitrogen. In the fixed objective order, the digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9874, 0.9885, 0.992, 0.9943 and 0.9874; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9655, 0.9667 and 0.8437. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the markers, not fractions of their atoms that are aromatic. Read-only RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 30, 33 and 25, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2. The corresponding Parent medians are 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 heavy atoms, and 3, 4, 4, 4 and 3 rings. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts in the current proposals are 655, 600, 588, 641 and 532, although many represent local ring edits or enlarged assemblies rather than independent useful core families. Conventional makeable-looking fragments coexist with N-Cl bonds, O-O bonds, imines, hydrazine-derived linkages, strained small rings, conjugated enlarged rings and highly charged oxygen environments. The digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0 on every objective; graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals respectively. Thus unspecified stereochemistry is a real representational gap, rather than evidence that the molecules are all achiral. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are mixed. The recorded scores support chemical associations within these samples; they do not establish a synthesis, a binding pose, or a causal contribution from any particular generator edit.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant upper family has a phenyl ring joining a diazine bearing an imidate or imine to a conjugated seven-member oxygen ring. The two highest digest examples each have 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic six-member rings and one nonaromatic seven-member oxepin-like ring. Other high entries replace the imidate with an amidine-containing aryl ether, change diazine nitrogen positions, or use a methoxyindole-carbonyl-imidazole-pyridyl assembly. These are moderately sized, largely unsaturated molecules, with polar groups placed on an extended ring framework. Their functional groups are chemically recognizable, but the imidates, imines and conjugated enol-ether ring make stability and synthetic handling less routine than for ordinary aryl amides. The full proposal median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; tiny fragments and much larger branched structures also occur. Compared with the Parent, the upper chemistry shifts from fused aza-ring/amide and unusual sulfur-containing families toward linked diazine/oxygen-ring imidates. The median aromatic-ring count falls from three in the Parent to two here, while median total ring count stays at three.
liabilities: The leading imidate/imine and conjugated oxygen-ring combinations warrant scrutiny for hydrolysis, tautomerism and chemical stability; their recorded scores do not measure these properties.

Late examples introduce ring expansion, a small imine-containing ring or thiol substitution without retaining the highest recorded scores. Increased ring or heteroatom complexity is not itself evidence of improved chemistry.
The full proposals include N-Cl and O-O bonds, and the large low-score assemblies can contain multiple unspecified stereocentres.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the connected aromatic framework and polar handles shared by the upper families; the largest poor examples lack their moderate size and limited elaboration. Those features are not preserved consistently across the output.

The upper excerpt shows conventional carbonyl chemistry mainly in a separate indole family, while the dominant linked-ring series relies on imidates, imines and amidines. Equally favorable, chemically varied polar-group arrangements within that same linked framework are not established by the shown molecules.

Methoxy or other alkoxy groups, halogens and a terminal aryl formaldimine recur. The highest example has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-member rings, but also an O-N(Cl)-ethyl substituent containing both N-O and N-Cl bonds. A simpler dimethoxy member has 24 heavy atoms. The fused aza core, arylamine link and ordinary ethers are plausible synthetic building blocks; the N-chlorinated hydroxylamine ether and formaldimine are less conventional final medicinal functionality. Another trajectory ends with nitrogen-dense fused systems, small fused rings and multiple explicitly negative oxygens. liabilities: N-Cl-bearing hydroxylamine ethers and terminal methylene imines introduce reactive functionality into the strongest-scoring family. Even the simpler dimethoxy analogue retains the imine.

Some final structures combine heavily fused small rings with alkoxide-like and N-O anions; the cited multiply negative molecule has no accompanying counterion in its SMILES. Charge and valence validity do not establish a plausible dominant chemical state.
The full optimizer set contains 121 molecules with an O-O bond, and its charged-marker rate is 0.2264. These features are materially present rather than isolated textual curiosities.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring sulfonyl or nitrogen-rich structures lack the specific aryl-NH-diazine connection and alkoxy substitution context shared by the upper molecules. Total aromaticity and nitrogen content do not substitute for this local arrangement.

The highest excerpt does not show broad coverage of different cores retaining an equally favorable attachment pattern; it mostly repeats one aza-aromatic family with peripheral variations. Chemically conservative alternatives to its reactive peripheral groups are only partially represented.

transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local bonding environments while modifying otherwise useful molecular cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make candidate construction sensitive to complete local functional-group environments, including the atoms bonded to nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and halogens. Retain access to conventional stable alternatives when varying an accepted core, so exploration does not depend on adding reactive heteroatom-halogen or heteroatom-heteroatom bonds. Learn any objective-value tradeoff from accepted feedback; these chemical concerns alone do not establish that blanket exclusions would improve scores.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve stereochemical assignments when constructing or changing potentially stereogenic centres, and make chemically feasible configurations available as distinct alternatives where the evaluation interface distinguishes them. transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper molecules include a ten-member conjugated aza-lactam marked aromatic by graph perception, a seven-member cyclic cumulene, aziridine-containing polycycles and several heavily fused small-ring systems. transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently constrain conjugation and ring geometry to chemically credible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore ring size, fusion, bond order and saturation with attention to the resulting geometry and functional-group compatibility. Keep conventional ring alternatives available while preserving useful attachment positions, and distinguish changes in ring topology from peripheral decoration. Aromatic notation and valence sanitization should not be treated as proof of a feasible conformation or easy synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A fluorinated urea/hydrazine pair has the same C14H17F3IN3O3 formula but scores 0.49702898037063575 and 0.42289529223448297 when fluorine is distributed differently between chain and aryl ring. Adding a consecutive nitrogen to a related chain gives 0.1359300194081745 instead of 0.4779789711749196. Elsewhere, two ring-nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coordinated alternatives for functional-group orientation, linker position and heteroatom placement while retaining a coherent core and comparable molecular scale. Distinguish accessible amines from amide, sulfonamide, aromatic and hydrazine nitrogen rather than treating element count as the relevant chemical property. transferable_gaps.evidence: The zero-score excerpts include methane, acetylene, a 25-heavy-atom acyclic polyamine and 70- or 83-heavy-atom multigroup assemblies. transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing moves do not consistently preserve a useful connected arrangement of rings, linkers and polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make growth, contraction and linker changes preserve a recognizable connected core and the relationships among its aromatic, amine and carbonyl groups. Maintain alternatives at multiple chemically coherent scales, with current accepted observations determining the useful size range. Treat fragmentation to tiny pieces and wholesale concatenation as distinct chemistry from controlled local elaboration.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent molecular prior and chooses its prepared checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid, connected, distinct molecular yield, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts an adaptable copy of that prior and an accepted-only archive; trajectory-balance updates with a learned normalizer and fixed-prior regularization transfer real graph feedback into later neural sampling. One direct neural batch alternates with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population and supply a protected descendant at the first graph handoff. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations construct temporary novel offspring pools, and accepted-score fingerprint posterior function draws choose the remaining evaluations. The atom-replacement mutation currently changes one element at one site, so moving a ring nitrogen while retaining composition requires multiple separately sampled substitutions.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with a direct positional exchange between a pyridine-like nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same aromatic six-member ring. The exchange moves the nitrogen while preserving the formula, ring connectivity and substituent attachment positions, making a new local arrangement available in one edit. Earlier Children in this lineage changed prior preparation, replay, flow credit or neural sampling. This Child changes graph generation. A previous graph-walk experiment established that this exchange can yield scored positional isomers but exposed very few of them and missed its score target; the new question is whether the Parent's larger temporary pools and posterior selection turn that same positional channel into useful accepted descendants.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per objective. The molecules include linked and fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, aryl sulfonamides, lactams, ethers, imidates and fluorinated urea/hydrazine chains. This is broad chemical exploration with concentrated upper-score families, rather than a shortage of rings or nitrogen. In the fixed objective order, the digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9874, 0.9885, 0.992, 0.9943 and 0.9874; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9655, 0.9667 and 0.8437. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the markers, not fractions of their atoms that are aromatic. Read-only RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 30, 33 and 25, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2. The corresponding Parent medians are 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 heavy atoms, and 3, 4, 4, 4 and 3 rings. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts in the current proposals are 655, 600, 588, 641 and 532, although many represent local ring edits or enlarged assemblies rather than independent useful core families. Conventional makeable-looking fragments coexist with N-Cl bonds, O-O bonds, imines, hydrazine-derived linkages, strained small rings, conjugated enlarged rings and highly charged oxygen environments. The digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0 on every objective; graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals respectively. Thus unspecified stereochemistry is a real representational gap, rather than evidence that the molecules are all achiral. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are mixed. The recorded scores support chemical associations within these samples; they do not establish a synthesis, a binding pose, or a causal contribution from any particular generator edit.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant upper family has a phenyl ring joining a diazine bearing an imidate or imine to a conjugated seven-member oxygen ring. The two highest digest examples each have 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic six-member rings and one nonaromatic seven-member oxepin-like ring. Other high entries replace the imidate with an amidine-containing aryl ether, change diazine nitrogen positions, or use a methoxyindole-carbonyl-imidazole-pyridyl assembly. These are moderately sized, largely unsaturated molecules, with polar groups placed on an extended ring framework. Their functional groups are chemically recognizable, but the imidates, imines and conjugated enol-ether ring make stability and synthetic handling less routine than for ordinary aryl amides. The full proposal median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; tiny fragments and much larger branched structures also occur. Compared with the Parent, the upper chemistry shifts from fused aza-ring/amide and unusual sulfur-containing families toward linked diazine/oxygen-ring imidates. The median aromatic-ring count falls from three in the Parent to two here, while median total ring count stays at three.
liabilities: The leading imidate/imine and conjugated oxygen-ring combinations warrant scrutiny for hydrolysis, tautomerism and chemical stability; their recorded scores do not measure these properties.
